title: Does a roof replacement require a permit in NH?
body_markdown:
A roof replacement in NH requires a permit when your municipality requires one for the work you plan to do; do not assume every town treats reroofing the same way. Before scheduling tear-off in 2026, confirm the requirement with your local building department and put responsibility for the application in your contract. Permit approval does not replace a clear installation scope or careful workmanship.


**TL;DR**

- Roof replacement permit NH requirements need confirmation from your local building department before tear-off.
- Prescott Roofing serves Southern New Hampshire homeowners planning residential roof replacement; clarify permit responsibilities when requesting an estimate.
- Your written estimate should identify who handles the permit, required inspections, and changes to the approved scope.
- A permit addresses approval; your contract still needs to explain materials, flashing, deck repairs, and cleanup.


## Does a roof replacement require a permit in NH?

**Get an address-specific answer from the building department before work starts.** Describe the actual replacement, not simply a roofing project. Removing shingles, replacing damaged decking, changing materials, and altering the roof structure are different scopes of work.

For a homeowner-paid replacement in 2026, use this sequence:

1. **Describe the scope.** Give the property address, existing roof covering, proposed covering, and whether the contractor plans a full tear-off.
2. **Confirm the requirement.** Ask whether that scope needs a building permit, additional review, or inspections.
3. **Assign responsibility.** Put the applicant, submission duties, and inspection coordination in the written agreement.
4. **Verify authorization.** If a permit is required, confirm it has been issued before the work it covers begins.
5. **Keep the closeout records.** Obtain the permit information and any required inspection results for your house records.

The [permit approval-to-tear-off workflow](https://prescottroofingnh.com/blog/permit-approval-to-tear-off-complete-nh-workflow) explains how approval fits into replacement planning. Treat the town's answer for your address and scope as the starting point, rather than another homeowner's experience.

## Why this matters

A permit question belongs in your contractor comparison, not in a conversation after the old roof comes off. You need to know who handles the paperwork and whether an inspection affects when the crew can cover the roof deck.

For Southern New Hampshire homeowners, the practical issue is accountability. A statement such as permits handled is incomplete unless the agreement identifies what that includes and who follows through.

**A complete roofing decision needs both approval clarity and installation clarity.** Neither substitutes for the other. An issued permit does not explain whether the estimate includes new step flashing, disposal, or repairs to damaged wood.

## Why roof replacement permit requirements vary

The building department needs enough detail to classify your project. These are the points to describe when asking about a 2026 replacement:

- **Municipality and property address.** Ask the department responsible for the actual property, whether it is in Manchester, Nashua, Bedford, or another town.
- **Removal or overlay.** State whether the crew will remove the existing roofing or install another covering over it.
- **Roof deck work.** Explain whether the plan includes replacing sheathing, the wood panels beneath the roofing.
- **Material changes.** Identify the existing and proposed covering, especially when switching between different roofing systems.
- **Structural changes.** Separate ordinary covering replacement from changes to rafters, roof shape, or openings.
- **Property restrictions.** Ask whether historic-district review or another property-specific approval applies.

This list is a preparation checklist, not a statement that every item triggers a permit. Have the department identify the requirement for your combination of work.

If the contractor changes the scope after the initial inquiry, confirm whether the original answer still applies. Approval for one description of work should not be treated as approval for an expanded project.

## What should you tell the building department?

Start with a plain description you can also use when requesting estimates. For example, describe a homeowner-paid replacement involving removal of the existing shingles and installation of a new asphalt-shingle roof, with concealed deck damage addressed if discovered. Adjust that description to match your house; do not submit assumptions as confirmed conditions.

Keep these details together:

| Project detail | What to provide | Why it helps |
|---|---|---|
| Property | Street address and type of residence | Identifies the project being reviewed |
| Existing roof | Current covering and known roof layers | Clarifies what the contractor intends to remove |
| Proposed work | Tear-off, new covering, and related work | Defines the planned replacement |
| Wood repairs | Known damage and proposed repair approach | Separates covering work from underlying repairs |
| Roof changes | Planned openings or structural alterations | Flags work beyond a like-for-like replacement |
| Applicant | Who intends to submit the paperwork | Clarifies responsibility before scheduling |

You do not need to diagnose concealed conditions yourself. State what is known, identify what remains uncertain, and ask how discoveries during tear-off should be handled.

Request a written response or retain the department's published guidance with your project notes. Record the date and the scope you described so the answer stays connected to the right work.

## Who should handle the roof permit: you or the contractor?

**Choose an arrangement the building department allows, then document it.** Do not assume that signing a roofing contract automatically assigns permit duties to the contractor or that a homeowner application removes the contractor's obligations.

Both arrangements need clear boundaries:

| Arrangement | Best for | Practical benefit | Limitation to resolve |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contractor handles submission | Homeowners who want application tasks coordinated with installation | Keeps scope information and scheduling with the installer | The contract must explain submission, inspection coordination, and closeout |
| Homeowner handles submission, where allowed | Homeowners prepared to manage the department's application process | Gives the homeowner direct control of the submission | The homeowner must obtain accurate technical information and coordinate with the contractor |

If you handle the application, ask the department what responsibilities you accept as the applicant. Never sign a description that does not match the agreed work.

If the contractor handles it, request the permit identifier once issued and ask how you will receive inspection records. A promise to take care of everything is not a substitute for a defined task in the contract.

## What should your roof replacement estimate say about permits?

A useful 2026 estimate makes permit responsibility easy to find. It should distinguish the application from the installation and explain how approval requirements affect scheduling.

Ask for these points in writing:

- **Permit responsibility:** Who confirms the requirement and submits the application?
- **Permit charges:** Does the proposal include applicable permit charges, or treat them separately?
- **Inspection coordination:** Who requests required inspections and communicates with the building department?
- **Start conditions:** What must happen before the crew begins tear-off?
- **Scope changes:** Who checks whether newly discovered work needs revised approval?
- **Closeout documents:** What records will you receive when the project is complete?

Then read the roofing scope itself. Look for the existing material removal, underlayment, roof-edge details, flashing, ventilation work, wood-repair procedure, debris removal, and property cleanup.

Step flashing is the overlapping metal used where a sloped roof meets a wall. An estimate should explain whether that detail is being replaced or retained, rather than leaving you to assume that a new roof includes every adjacent component.

Prescott Roofing is a fit for Southern New Hampshire homeowners seeking residential roof replacement. When requesting an inspection, ask for the permit responsibility and proposed installation scope to be addressed together; that is how you compare the work rather than just the headline proposal.

**[Request an inspection](https://prescottroofingnh.com/contact)**


Submitting an inspection request does not mean an appointment is booked. Wait for confirmation of the appointment details before arranging access or changing your schedule.

## How should permit approval fit into the work schedule?

Plan the sequence before choosing a tear-off date. In 2026, the sound approach is to confirm requirements, obtain any necessary approval, coordinate required inspections, and retain the completion records.

Use these phases when discussing the schedule:

- **Scope confirmation:** Make sure the application and contract describe the same project.
- **Permit approval:** Confirm any required authorization is issued before the covered work starts.
- **Inspection coordination:** Ask whether the department needs to see work before it is concealed.
- **Project closeout:** Collect the required results and resolve any open items.


![Roof replacement sequence from scope confirmation through permit approval, inspection coordination, and project closeout](https://media.get-ryze.ai/workspace-article-images-public/9d4bf594-d595-48f5-915a-68cf8d8e12e3/body-e9485052223b3dc24f3fd043bf4e1198.png)

*Agree on approval and inspection responsibilities before choosing the tear-off date.*


Do not confuse an application receipt with an issued permit. Ask the building department what document authorizes the work and whether any conditions must be satisfied first.

Also ask the contractor how the crew will protect the house if an inspection interrupts the installation sequence. The answer should describe the work plan without promising that municipal scheduling is under the contractor's control.

## Can I replace the shingles without changing the roof structure?

Replacing shingles without structural changes does not, by itself, establish whether your town requires a permit. Describe the covering replacement accurately and ask the local building department to confirm the requirement.

Keep structural work separate in the estimate. Replacing deteriorated roof sheathing is not the same description as changing rafters or altering the roofline, and your paperwork should not blur those tasks together.

## What happens if the crew finds damaged decking?

Damaged decking needs a documented repair decision before it is covered with the new roofing system. Ask the contractor to photograph the affected area, explain the proposed repair, and obtain your authorization under the contract's change procedure.

The contractor or applicant should also confirm whether the discovery changes permit or inspection requirements. Do not assume that concealed damage is automatically covered by the original project description.

## Does a permit mean the roofing estimate is complete?

A permit does not establish what your contractor has agreed to install. The estimate and contract must still define the materials, preparation, flashing, repair allowances, exclusions, and cleanup.

Compare those details before selecting a contractor. A proposal with clear permit language can still leave important roof work undefined.

## FAQ


**Do I need a permit to replace my roof in New Hampshire in 2026?**

Confirm the requirement with the building department responsible for your property before work starts. Give the address and full scope, including tear-off, material changes, and any planned deck or structural work.

**Who should pull the permit for my roof replacement?**

The applicant should be someone the local building department allows to apply, with responsibilities stated in your contract. Confirm who submits the application, coordinates inspections, and provides the closeout records.

**Can my roofer start while the permit application is pending?**

Do not authorize work that requires a permit until the required authorization is issued. An application submission is not the same as approval to begin.

**Does replacing only the shingles make the job permit-exempt?**

Do not assume a shingles-only replacement is permit-exempt. Describe the project to your local building department and ask for confirmation of the applicable requirement.

**Should my roof replacement estimate include permit information?**

Your estimate should identify permit responsibility and explain whether applicable permit charges are included or separate. It should also identify who handles required inspections and changes to the approved scope.

**What should I keep after a permitted roof replacement?**

Keep the issued permit information, required inspection results, signed contract, and approved changes. Store those records with the replacement scope and project photographs.

**Can Prescott Roofing inspect my roof before I choose a replacement contractor?**

You can request a residential roofing inspection from Prescott Roofing. A request is not a confirmed appointment; confirm scheduling and the inspection details directly.


## One last thing

**An application receipt is not proof that a permit has been issued.** Before tear-off, match the authorized address and scope to your signed contract, then confirm who is responsible for any remaining inspection steps.

That document check is useful even when the project looks straightforward. It catches a mismatch while the old roof is still protecting your house, rather than after the crew has started removing it.
